target_body: Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

memory_block.body: Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

answer.rationale:
The two acute, measurable declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the inherited record points most directly at friction reduction in the onboarding path (memory_86: shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value; memory_31: cutting signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift). That targets both symptoms with one slot, and unlike promotional_pricing it does not carry a known retention penalty. I am deliberately not chasing the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 shows promo pricing buys acquisition and revenue while materially damaging 30-day retention, which is exactly the wrong trade against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but is scoped to established customers and does nothing for the activation/onboarding drop; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not where the deterioration is.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the load-bearing evidence for the action I intend, and because both are stated purely in early-funnel terms — completion, time-to-value, first-week activation — with no evidence about retention, expansion, or revenue quality further out. That is the same shape of claim that memory_73 turned out to conceal a downstream cost in: a real top-of-funnel win that did not survive to 30 days. Removing required fields and steps can also shift who gets in and how well qualified they are, so the archived records need to be checked for whether any downstream metric was measured at all, what the sample and duration were, and whether the 'durable' lift in memory_31 was actually tracked past week one. I also want to know whether memory_86 and memory_31 overlap — if they are the same friction-reduction lever measured twice, the evidence base is thinner than six memories suggests, and the remaining headroom may already have been consumed on day 12 and day 52.

Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: memory_91 (activation messaging) is the freshest record at day 61 and is a live alternative for the activation decline specifically; if verification shows the onboarding levers are already exhausted or were never measured past week one, activation_messaging becomes the better use of the slot. Nothing in the inherited memory establishes that any of these interventions was tested against an aggressive-pricing competitive environment, so the prior conditions may not hold on day 76. I am running this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, with 30-day retention and qualified-revenue guardrails instrumented up front, so that a repeat of the memory_73 pattern — front-loaded gains masking downstream erosion — would be caught before it is generalized into memory.
